The fold and the two Smith charts

One element read out: u = g·ln s + a, Γ = tanh(u/2), Γ_SCALE east–west, Γ_ADD north–south, and the firing defect. A picture shows a structure; it is not evidence that the structure means anything beyond its definition.

← ADD:SCALE:SIGN gallery

About this visual

What you are looking at. The read-out of one element: its word u = g·ln s + a, its fold Γ = tanh(u/2), and its place on the two orthogonal Smith charts. Left: the unit disc with Γ_SCALE = tanh(½·ln s) on the east–west axis and Γ_ADD = tanh(½·a) on the north–south axis. Right: u over the (add, ln s) plane, and below it the firing defect (g − 1)·ln s against ln s.

How to read it. Move the sliders or click the right-hand map to set (add, ln s). Flip the sign: the point is drawn filled for g = +1 and as a ring for g = −1, and its quadrant gets a prime (′). The defect plot has two lines: g = +1 is flat at zero, g = −1 is −2·ln s.

What it shows. That SIGN only matters to the fold where SCALE is not 1: at s = 1 the defect is zero for either sign. The quadrant letters follow the rings: north = add ≥ 0, east = scale ≥ 1 (at version 0.1 the two letters were swapped; the page's self-check found it, test and ledger X-71).

What it does not show. The fold of a composite: u of a product is not the sum of the factors' u, and this page does not combine elements (that is the first page). Γ here is the real-axis form of the Smith-chart fold, not a full complex chart.

Numbers to check. Γ_SCALE = tanh(½·ln s), Γ_ADD = tanh(½·a), Γ = tanh(½·(g·ln s + a)); the defect is (g−1)·ln s, which is −2·ln s for g = −1. At (a, s, g) = (3, 0.25, +1): Γ_SCALE = −0.6, Γ_ADD = 0.905, quadrant NW (add north, scale below 1 west).

running self-check…

Code and data. Everything shown is recomputed in the browser by ass.js (composition, inverse, commutator, word, fold, the Long Path and exact rational arithmetic) and compared with the numbers the Python engine produced (ass_data.js); the result is printed above. Light and dark follow the system.

  • Wikipedia, "Commutator": the group commutator [x, y] = x⁻¹y⁻¹xy used here.
